title: Connectedness of extremal Green level sets
exact_target: Does permitting disconnected compact sets increase the largest Green-level length exponent, and can a connected set attain the optimum?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
For a compact set $E\subset\mathbb C$ of positive
logarithmic capacity, let $G_E$ be the Green
function with pole at infinity of the unbounded
complementary component, extended by zero elsewhere.
Assume regularity, meaning that this extension
is continuous. Normalize
$G_E(z)-\log|z|\to-\log\operatorname{cap}(E)$
as $z\to\infty$.
Define
\[
 \beta_E=\limsup_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}
 \frac{\log\mathcal H^1\{z:G_E(z)=\varepsilon\}}
                         {-\log\varepsilon},
\]
where $\mathcal H^1$ measures the total length
of all level-curve components.

Compare
$\beta_{\mathrm{all}}=\sup_E\beta_E$, over
all such regular compact sets, with
$\beta_{\mathrm{conn}}=\sup_{E\ \mathrm{connected}}\beta_E$.
Is the unrestricted supremum attained on
connected sets? In particular, determine whether
$\beta_{\mathrm{all}}=\beta_{\mathrm{conn}}$,
so that allowing disconnected compact sets
does not increase the optimal exponent.

Distinguish this equality of suprema from the
stronger attainment question: does there exist
one regular connected compact set $E_*$ with
$\beta_{E_*}=\beta_{\mathrm{all}}$? The
source's wording invites investigation of both.
A comparison of suprema may be established
by connected examples approaching every
unrestricted exponent without producing a
single maximizer.
Disconnected sets may have arbitrarily many
components. No restriction on component size,
separation, boundary regularity beyond the
Green-function condition, or finite boundary
length is imposed.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Does permitting disconnected compact sets increase the largest Green-level length exponent, and can a connected set attain the optimum?
